mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the same month of the rate hike, with a p-value > 0.05 in a t-test versus pre-hike month returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% for two consecutive months is accompanied by a decline in S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to higher labor market rigidity and reduced corporate hiring expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive during the two-month UNRATE expansion, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the HOUST industrial production index exceeds 1,000 for three consecutive months, indicating accelerating output growth, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as market anticipates stronger earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the three-month expansion window, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO below 100 (monthly) suggests contracting supply capacity, which raises the cost of production and compresses S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 100 for less than one month, or 20-day forward returns are positive during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE over a 3-month period indicate dual easing, which amplifies equity valuation expansion and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05) during the easing period.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS (monthly employment) exceeds 140,000 for two consecutive months in a labor market recovery, it signals labor market absorption, prompting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the employment expansion, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in GDPC1 (real GDP) above 2% for four consecutive quarters is associated with stronger earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns in the following quarter.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2% for 4 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative during the growth quarter, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 4%, S&P 500 5-day forward returns tend to be negative due to higher discounting of future cash flows, regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not detectable in a rolling window analysis.
